c35.question: Explain how Kafka consumer groups work.
c35.answer: A Kafka consumer group is a set of consumers that collectively consume messages from a topic. Its purpose is to enable scalable and fault-tolerant message processing. Consumer groups balance the load by distributing partitions among members, ensuring each partition is consumed by exactly one consumer. The group coordinator (typically a Kafka broker) manages assignments and synchronizes consumers. It tracks offsets and handles rebalancing if members join or leave. Partition assignment strategies like range or round-robin determine how partitions are allocated. Consumers synchronize through the coordinator to maintain consistent offset tracking and ensure no message is missed or duplicated.
